title: England vs. Spain in the Nations League
seoTitle: England vs. Spain: Nations League Clash at Wembley
subtitle: The clash between the World Champion and the World Cup third-place team is set for Wembley
excerpt: England and Spain will face off in the opening round of the 2026/27 Nations League at Wembley, London, at 3:45 PM BRT.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The match between England and Spain, in the first round of the 2026/27 Nations League, will be played at Wembley, in London, at 3:45 PM (Brasília time). The clash brings together the reigning world champion and the third-placed team from the last World Cup.

What's at Stake in the Nations League Opening Round

England and Spain face off this Saturday, September 26, 2026, at Wembley. The match is part of the inaugural phase of the 2026/27 Nations League, with England as the third-placed team in the last World Cup and Spain as the world champion.

Match Details and Broadcast Information

The game kicks off at 3:45 PM (Brasília time) and will be broadcast by ESPN and the Disney+ platform. The referee will be Davide Massa from Italy.

England Squad and Injuries Affecting the Team

Thomas Tuchel has called up an England squad that includes Pickford, Quansah, Konsa, Guéhi, and O'Reilly in defense, Elliot Anderson, Bellingham, and Morgan Rogers in midfield, and Saka, Gordon, and Kane up front. Players Cole Palmer, Declan Rice, Mainoo, Tino Livramento, and Rashford have been cut from the squad.

Spain Squad and Last-Minute Changes

Luis de la Fuente maintains most of the players who won the World Cup. However, Pedro Porro is injured, and Pedri is doubtful for the match. Eric García and Marc Pubill could fill the right-back position. The central defensive partnership could be Pau Cubarsí and Laporte, while Cucurella remains a starter on the left.

Coaches' Expectations and Comments

De la Fuente emphasizes the importance of not entering with arrogance, as the Nations League has less prestige than the World Cup, but still demands commitment and victory. Thomas Tuchel, in turn, dismissed the possibility that British fans would feel insecure after the World Cup semi-final exit, pointing out that the demand for tickets indicates strong home support.

With information from ge, LANCE!.
